purpose: Verify the locally integrated Qwen3-ASR capability interface without substituting upstream model-card claims.

fixture.description: Local 139.284-second two-speaker Mandarin-English code-switch and Sichuanese/filler probe.

observations.automatic_language_interface: Both checkpoints emitted one language label when passed no language hint, but the labels disagreed on the same mixed-language recording. The label applies to the whole processing container and is not localized code-switch metadata.
observations.code_switch_interface: Both outputs contain Han and Latin text in the same segment. This verifies mixed-script retention through the local adapter, not code-switch accuracy.
observations.dialect_interface: The 1.7B output retained the Sichuanese lexeme 耍啥子 while 0.6B rendered 刷啥子. One unlabelled clip cannot validate dialect breadth or error rate.
observations.speaker_interface: Both normalized outputs contain speaker=null; Qwen3-ASR supplies no diarization through this adapter.
observations.time_interface: Each output contains one 0.0-139.284 second processing-container interval and no speech, word, or character timestamps. Timing must come from VAD, diarization, or forced alignment.
observations.verbatim_interface: No filler-specific or verbatim mode was exercised. Filler preservation remains a transcript-quality measurement, not a native output capability.

decision: Use Qwen3-ASR as a fast transcript worker behind an external timing/speaker plan. Automatic language output exists but is not a reliable code-switch locator or routing signal on this probe; prefer an explicit primary-language hint when known.
